interpretation: All five original jobs completed successfully at source ca1e36a0773e9c5e253ed040a68f488b8a7353ad, including actual hosted Chrome, Firefox and Microsoft Edge production Web-to-native flows. Complete official raw logs for all five jobs are independently hashed. Edge retains browser_product=edge and the producer engine value chrome.

All three browsers and native fixtures exit zero, with no runner validation failures. Each original flow records approximately 36 seconds at approximately 10 decoded frames per second, seven steady renewals with valid sequence and zero response observations after close. Original thresholds and lifetime budgets are unchanged.

Original production Web UI, real local WebRTC/VP8/Opus, owned input recording and exact SCTP tempfile transfers pass. Owned processes stop without forced termination, the private directories and temporary database are removed, server threads join, capture resets and audio cleanup succeeds. Capture remains synthetic; no installed-platform, hardware media, HDR or physical scanout acceptance is claimed.

The new published-receipts.json exists in each real browser artifact. All three source/run/attempt claims match. Each inventory has 14 exact public file entries after sanitization, and all 42 entries independently match actual byte length and SHA256, including the public progress JSONL. The inventory explicitly excludes its own file and the final runner result; those bytes are still independently hashed in the complete actual-file inventory.

Original progress_sha256 fields still cover private raw JSONL before sanitization and reserialization. Those three private-raw digests remain independently unverified because private bytes are absent; the successful public payload verification does not change their original meaning.

All six official ZIP digests, sizes and exact run/source identities match, and all 61 actual downloaded files are independently hashed. The 46 producer payload entries comprise 42 published browser entries and four release-site lock entries. Before, after locked metadata and after build Cargo.lock bytes match their receipts, together with the original zero-byte Cargo.lock.diff.

The original host terminal field Some(Transport), WebRtcClosed/AnswerNextOffer and PeerGuardCancelRequested diagnostics are retained verbatim. They do not replace the producer's final zero browser/native exit codes or successful original cleanup receipts.

Historical a1afd8b hosted success, f24b79f Firefox denial/timeout and 760f232/895614e native-build failures remain separate, unchanged exact-source evidence. No assertion, case, selector, timeout, public HTTPS trust, 60 ms ingress, 40 ms late, PTS/capture or Luanti 25 second threshold has been weakened. Full target and release acceptance are not claimed.
